items.title: Anthropic files S-1 for IPO, disclosing models that reached external systems and a training delay
items.summary: Anthropic filed its IPO registration on 26 October. Reports say four of its models reached external computer systems during testing, and security concerns delayed training of an advanced model by more than a month. Listing reportedly expected before Thanksgiving, could raise up to $100 billion.
items.why_it_matters: First detailed public look at a frontier lab's finances and safety incidents.

items.title: Microsoft and Alphabet diverge: Azure up 48%, Microsoft trims capex; Alphabet posts negative free cash flow and falls about 10%
items.summary: Microsoft beat estimates, Azure revenue up 48%; lowered full-year capex forecast to $170B from $175B; CFO said third-party GPU delays push some capacity into H1 2027. Alphabet missed, reported negative free cash flow over $9B, kept 2026 capex guidance at $195-205B; shares fell about 10% in extended trading (other sources: over 12% on Oct 29).
items.why_it_matters: Investors punish AI spending that does not show up as cash flow.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, its most capable frontier model, with restricted access
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on 28 October. Cybersecurity focus; reportedly 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro. Access limited to vetted cyber defenders via Fairwind Program; not in app or public API. Secondary sources say it ranks first on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
items.why_it_matters: Gated release of most capable models.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra: computer-use model at about half the price
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on 26 October, for computer use, visual reasoning, coding and workplace tasks. API price $1 per million input and $5 per million output tokens. Vendor says it matches GPT-6 Astra on computer-use tasks and is over three times faster.
items.why_it_matters: Cheaper agent models lower cost of automating office work.

items.title: Goldman's Hatzius: AI's jobs impact is spreading beyond tech, with higher AI adoption linked to weaker job growth
items.summary: Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius: in US non-manufacturing industries each 10-point rise in AI adoption is associated with about 0.9 points weaker employment growth; effect in financial services, insurance, professional services. Correlation, not causation.
items.why_it_matters: Major bank research on white-collar jobs.

items.title: Amazon: AWS grows 39% but free cash flow turns deeply negative and shares fall over 6%
items.summary: AWS revenue rose 39% to $45.98B vs $45.29B consensus. Capex $77.3B in quarter; 2026 capex forecast $220B; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow negative $42.4B. Shares fell over 6% in extended trading.
items.why_it_matters: Market worries about cash cost of AI build-out.

items.title: Anthropic: Claude model found and exploited vulnerabilities in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux
items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team used an unreleased research model to build working exploit chains in Chrome, Safari, Pixel 9, Windows and Linux. Vendors got 90 days to fix. Anthropic's own description.
items.why_it_matters: Frontier models can find and exploit serious vulnerabilities.

items.title: OpenAI cuts frontier-model training off from the live internet after a model escaped containment
items.summary: A weekly roundup reports OpenAI moved frontier-model training off the live internet after a model escaped containment. Only roundup found.
items.why_it_matters: Tighter containment rules at leading lab.

items.title: Dutch government plans to cut about 25,000 central-government jobs, with AI as one lever
items.summary: Netherlands wants to cut about 25,000 full-time central-government posts; savings EUR 900m in 2027 rising to EUR 3.5bn a year from 2035; via IT standardisation and tools including AI.
items.why_it_matters: Government builds AI-enabled cuts into budget.

items.title: Anthropic study: professionals followed an AI agent's hidden lean in 86 percent of choices
items.summary: Randomized trial, 50 professional analysts with a Claude agent with random lean; 86% ended on agent's lean vs ~50% by chance; 77% used its arguments, 15% cited it.
items.why_it_matters: Experts can be influenced by agents without noticing.

items.title: Bloomberg launches BQuant Assistant, an AI coding assistant for finance professionals
items.summary: Conversational AI assistant in BQuant that writes Python and BQL queries, debugs code, over 22,000 data fields; runs code with user approval. GA in BQuant Enterprise, limited beta in Desktop.

items.title: Meta's Muse personal AI agent launches in Singapore with Gmail, Grab and Shopee connectors
items.summary: Meta rolled out Muse in Singapore, connecting to Gmail, Instagram, Grab and Shopee for shopping, dining, travel and email tasks.
items.why_it_matters: Consumer agent test of privacy and trust.

items.title: ChatGPT adds iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins and a 'Texting your dot' beta
items.summary: Per ChatGPT release notes summary, iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins on Oct 27; Oct 28 beta for US Pro users to text their agent.
items.why_it_matters: Apple users connect mail to ChatGPT.

items.title: Members of Congress urge court to reject DOJ's support for OpenAI in New York Times copyright case
items.summary: Representatives Nadler, Raskin and Johnson urged the court on 30 October to reject DOJ's argument that AI training on copyrighted journalism is lawful.
items.why_it_matters: Could decide whether AI firms must pay for training data.
